title: Attention in ten cards
subtitle: An example pack showing every card type the player supports.

cards.title: Attention
cards.caption: Every word gets to look at every other word.
cards.body: You read a sentence one word at a time. A model does not. It drops every word on the table at once and lets each one ask the rest: *who here matters to me?* That one move is **attention**.

cards.title: Three parts
cards.caption: Tap the numbered spots to see what each part does.

hotspots.label: Query
hotspots.body: What this word is looking for.

hotspots.label: Value
hotspots.body: What gets passed along once a match is found.

cards.caption: How many words can a small model attend to at once?
cards.body: The window is the number of tokens the model can hold in view. The on-device 4B model here runs with a 16K window on recent Apple devices.

guess.prompt: Guess the window size, in tokens.

cards.question: In attention, what does the **query** represent?

choices.text: What the current word is looking for
choices.why: The query is the question a word asks of the others.

choices.text: The final answer the model prints
choices.why: That comes much later, after many layers.

choices.text: A list of every word in the training data
choices.why: Attention works on the current input, not on the training set.

cards.text: Each word compares its {{query}} against every other word's {{key}}, then collects their {{values}}.

cards.summary: Attention lets every token weigh every other token. Query asks, key answers, value carries. The window caps how many tokens can take part at once.

cards.prompt: Put the steps of one attention pass in order.
items: Turn each token into a query, a key and a value
Compare the query with every key
Add up the values by those weights

cards.title: Weigh the words
cards.html:
Drag the slider to give bank more weight from either neighbour, then decide the meaning.

the river bank money

river 50% · money 50%

cards.prompt: In one or two sentences, explain why a model needs attention at all.
cards.model_answer: Words change meaning depending on their neighbours, so each token has to look at the others to decide what it means here. Attention is the step that lets every token weigh every other one.
cards.rubric: Meaning depends on context; tokens look at each other; weights decide how much each one counts.
